next_action: Human steps only: npm run ship, then attach a domain and submit it to Google Search Console. No code change is blocking anything.
corrections: The figure previously reported here and to directory listings (4,485 requests / 2,926 payment challenges) was NOT demand. Every 402 counted as a paid_attempt, so crawlers touching a paid path were recorded as callers trying to buy.
paid_attempts now means a request that actually carried a payment payload; challenges has its own column. Rows written before 2026-09-16 overstate paid_attempts and should not be quoted.
'Payment flow verified' previously recorded here was overstated: the x402 402 challenge was verified, a settlement was not.
notes: x402 v1 payers were rejected by construction until 2026-09-16: requirements went out in a v2-only header and payment came back in a header the v2 server never read. Fixed in src/v1compat.js.
A probe forwarding an MPP credential could settle on-chain against a discarded response, charging a caller for nothing. Fixed; the probe now carries no credential of any rail.

A /price/crypto endpoint and a / route existed in production on 2026-09-16 but were never committed to this repo - deployed by a separate ChatGPT session working from ~/penniless-work/penniless-market-rates. A deploy from this repo replaced them.
Two assistants deploying to the same Worker without committing will keep overwriting each other. Commit before deploying.

Demand assessment unchanged: all nine tools are things a caller can do locally for free or via free keyless public APIs, so no agent has an economic reason to fund a wallet for them. The rails are not the reason there is no revenue.
